source.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
source.authors: Yipeng Zhao; Qi-Shun Yang; Shenzhe Zhu; Shu Yang; Di Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extracts a refusal/compliance direction and tests a training-time penalty on displacement along it, reporting safety behavior. This is a different intervention from ablating or adding the original harmful-minus-harmless direction.
record.gate_note: The paper does not directly ablate or add a refusal direction at inference, and does not test weight-edit removal or jailbreak suppression. Its safety direction is a per-layer difference between templated refusal and compliance responses to the same harmful prompts, not the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction contrast. Direction profiles and diagnostic values used to choose layers or penalty scopes are not recorded as outcome rows. The study reports behavioral outcomes for reasoning fine-tuning and the safety-direction penalty, and probe results separating harm perception from refusal decisions.
record.test_reason: The probe results bear on V5 in a new setting, benign reasoning fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct. A linear harm-perception probe stays near-perfect while the refuse/fulfill decision probe collapses to the majority-class baseline. The rest of the paper does not test V1. Its direction is a refusal-minus-compliance contrast over responses, not the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. The direction is never ablated or added at inference. It is used as a training-time penalty target whose own performance is reported (SDP, T4-like).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add: authors frame RIM as a decision failure, not a perception failure (harm still recognized, refusal not executed). Add: SDP restores safety without safety training data, a reference policy or inference-time intervention.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a per-layer refusal-minus-compliance direction from paired responses to harmful prompts and penalizes its displacement during reasoning fine-tuning. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction for direct inference-time ablation or addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on model and training setting: SDP on the initial scope restores safety for 7B but not 3B; expanding 3B scope to {L19, . . . , L32} restores it, while expanding 7B beyond its rCKA > 1 boundary worsens safety. The penalty weight also changes safety and reasoning outcomes (Appendix D.7).

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning displacement along a refusal-minus-compliance response direction correlates with per-prompt harmfulness increase (ρ=0.475 for 3B, 0.277 for 7B). This direction is weakly negatively aligned with a reasoning direction (mean |cos_w| ≈ 0.13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss of refusal under benign fine-tuning tracks movement along a refusal/compliance response direction.

fits_no_version.finding: A training-time penalty on displacement along that direction restores the HEx-PHI harmfulness rate to the base level (3B 10.0%, 7B 11.3%). GPQA drops by 2 to 4 pp, and the result depends on the layer scope.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constraining a refusal direction during fine-tuning preserves refusal.

record.code_released: Code and data will be released upon publication.
record.problems: The direction uses a fixed refusal template and last-token representations. The authors explicitly caution that the geometric analysis is a local account, not a general causal characterization. SDP is tested on only two positive RIM settings for the main intervention; benchmark reasoning changes include GPQA decreases. HEx-PHI judgments use GPT-4o-mini, one judgment per prompt in the main evaluation, although the paper reports repeated-judging noise checks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out due to the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No inference-time ablation or addition of a harmful-minus-harmless direction; no refusal rate under such an intervention.
No single-direction versus multi-direction comparison. Multidimensional subspaces are mentioned only as future work.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants or base-to-instruct models.
No test of how refusal training shapes the direction.
AM-SFT models emit <think> traces, but no direction ablation or addition is done on them.

missing.what: Qwen2.5-14B: the safety-decision probe is not disrupted after AM-SFT (peak 0.97, above the 0.933 baseline), and there is no safety degradation. So the perception–decision dissociation arises only where RIM occurs.
67% of harmful <think> responses mention safety or ethics concerns in the trace. Behavioral evidence of recognition without refusal.
The probe conclusions are reported as unchanged at the prompt-encoding position and the mean-pooled position.

record.verdict_notes: The safety direction contrasts a fixed refusal template against compliance targets on the same AdvBench prompts. The authors explicitly distinguish it from Arditi's harmful-vs-harmless contrast. Only V5 gets a verdict, from probe decodability rather than causal intervention. The AM-SFT majority-class baselines for the decision probe are not reported numerically.

versions.untested_parts: No direct inference-time ablation or addition of the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction; no test that projecting it out of every layer and position removes refusal. The penalty is applied during fine-tuning, to a per-layer refusal/compliance direction measured at the last token.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration test.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No empirical comparison of a single direction with an affine space, cone, or multiple directions. The authors note multidimensional safety subspaces as future work.
Tests harmful-request perception and the model's refuse/fulfill decision on HEx-PHI prompts; does not establish a complete account of harmfulness judgment or decision-making.
No direction-transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models; directions are extracted separately for the tested models.
The paper varies reasoning fine-tuning settings and finds conditional RIM, but does not test whether refusal-training choices determine the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning-model checkpoints that reason before answering are evaluated as a distinct model type.

relationships.reason: Harm-perception probe accuracy stays at about 0.98 (r17, r18) while the refuse/fulfill probe falls to majority-class level (r19, r20). Harm recognition persists without the refusal decision. The evidence is correlational (decodability), not causal.

relation.reason: The study's own harm-perception and safety-decision probes (§3.4, C.4) test V5 directly. The SDP part uses the Arditi-style direction without testing V1.

tranche.reason: New setting: benign reasoning LoRA-SFT of Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct. Its own probe results bear on V5: harm stays decodable while the refuse/fulfill decision becomes undecodable. The refusal direction is otherwise used as a tool (the SDP penalty), so V1 is not tested.

source_check.notes: The record's code=y is wrong: code is promised only on publication. The intro's 'refusal rate drops from over 90% to random-chance' conflates probe accuracy with refusal rate. Actual HEx-PHI harmfulness goes 10.00->20.33 (3B) and 13.33->25.33 (7B). In 14B, with no RIM, the decision probe does not collapse (E.1). The decision probe reads the prompt-end state, while AM-SFT models often decide inside <think>.

statements.correction: arXiv:2608.23497: code and data 'will be released upon publication' (Appendix F; license table 'MIT (upon publication)'). Probe accuracies are 5-fold means with no SD or CI. Uncertainty is given only for AIME (±SD over 8 runs) and as Spearman p-values. Controls: majority-class baseline for the decision probe. Capability check: GPQA/AIME. Setting: LoRA r=16 SFT on 10k AM-DeepSeek examples.
statements.problem: The probe numbers and the collapse claim are correct (Appendix C.4, §3.4). The 'why' part is wrong for this study: the code is not released, and the V5 probe results carry no uncertainty.
